answer: Arrival-phase spread scoring. Each identity must space its first N actions across a required inter-arrival window shaped like a slow ocean swell; bursts collapsing into a single tick are flagged. Identity admission checks a per-window entropy floor on arrival timing. A sybil cluster pays in forced serialization: it can only launch one identity per window, so reaching K identities costs K windows of waiting, and early burst attempts forfeit the whole sonnet of queued registrations. Operators tune the floor with a saffron-coded threshold table published each epoch.
